proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived and independently reviewed the analytic full-continuum saddle point, certified arbitrary-accuracy frontier, original-record minimax transfer, strict information gain, and partial least-favorable-support characterization. A reverse-kernel proof defect was repaired using an auxiliary supplied-count kernel, and both cited substrates were retrieved and attested; final math and decision panels passed with no findings. The achieved subfield tier did not meet the field floor because of the narrow iid reset calibration model and absent practical non-corner computations; no Lean formalization or substrate promotion was attempted.
tldr: For the supplied iid two-state calibration class, the long-run causal policy contrast is \(B(u)h/\sqrt n\). Its all-estimator scaled squared-risk frontier converges uniformly on public compact domains to a concrete Gaussian--four-Poisson decision value. A full-continuum saddle point solves this value for \(0<c\le1\) and \(H\le\sqrt{4\mu(1-\mu)}\); certified finite primal and dual programs compute it to any requested accuracy throughout the public domain, and jitter averaging gives a total deterministic original-record attaining sequence. The canonical risk lies in \([0.10219817397550174,0.10219822795383387]\), improving on reward-only risk \(1/9\) by at least \(0.0089128831\). The corner prior has an exact computable zero-excess validity criterion and explicit exclusion regions; its remaining support-transition geometry is partially unresolved.
gap: Regular average-reward efficiency and bounded-mean minimax computation are established. The inspected primary literature does not give the concrete reward-neutral Gaussian--four-Poisson all-estimator contrast frontier, its continuum saddle point, and its original-record attainment. Search absence is bounded evidence, not a theorem.
fill: The paper solves the supplied full coefficient and reward boxes, combines analytic risk domination with arbitrary-tolerance certified programs, and transfers the result through a nuisance-preserving two-sided experiment comparison. The open support-geometry question identifies the unresolved optimizer boundary.
